1.title: Two Sum
1.notes:
Approach: Use a hash map to store previously seen numbers and their indices, allowing single-pass O(1) lookup for each element's complement.
Time: O(n)
Space: O(n)

15.title: 3Sum
15.notes:
Approach: Sort the array and use a three-pointer technique. Iterate through the array with a fixed element, and use a two-pointer approach for the remaining elements to find pairs that sum to the target. Skip duplicates to ensure the triplets are unique, and break early when the fixed element is positive.
Time: O(n^2)
Space: O(n) for the sorting overhead in Python (Timsort) or O(1) if sorting in-place without auxiliary space.

32.title: Longest Valid Parentheses
32.notes:
Approach: Maintain a stack storing indices, initialized with -1 as a base. Push indices of '(' and pop for ')', updating the maximum length using the index remaining at the top of the stack, or pushing the current index if the stack becomes empty.
Time: O(n)
Space: O(n)

100.title: Same Tree
100.notes:
Approach:
The problem is solved using a recursive depth-first traversal. We check if both nodes are null (equal), if only one of them is null (not equal), and if their values differ (not equal). If none of these conditions are met, we recursively check if their left and right subtrees are identical.

Time: O(N) where N is the number of nodes in the smaller tree, as we visit each node at most once.
Space: O(H) where H is the height of the tree, representing the maximum call stack depth (O(N) in the worst case of a completely unbalanced tree).

217.title: Contains Duplicate
217.notes:
Approach: Convert the list into a hash set and check if the size of the set is smaller than the original list length.
Time: O(N)
Space: O(N)

921.title: Minimum Add to Make Parentheses Valid

1254.title: Number of Closed Islands
1254.notes:
Approach: First, use DFS to sink (turn to 1) all land cells connected to the grid boundaries, as they cannot form closed islands. Then, iterate through the inner cells and perform DFS to count and sink each remaining isolated island of land.
Time: O(m * n)
Space: O(m * n)

1541.title: Minimum Insertions to Balance a Parentheses String
1541.notes:
An elegant greedy approach can be used to solve this problem. We can iterate through the string and keep track of two variables:
1. `insertions`: the number of characters we need to insert to balance the string.
2. `right_needed`: the number of right parentheses `)` we currently need to match the open parentheses `(` we have seen so far.

Since each `(` needs two `)` to balance:
- When we encounter a `(`, we need 2 more `)`. If our current `right_needed` is odd, it means there is a previous `(` that has only matched one `)`. Because we are now starting a new `(` group, we must immediately insert a `)` to complete the previous pair. Thus, we increment `insertions` by 1 and decrement `right_needed` by 1 before adding the 2 needed for the new `(`.
- When we encounter a `)`, we decrement `right_needed` by 1. If `right_needed` becomes `-1` (meaning we got a `)` but had no unmatched `(`), we must insert a `(` before it. A `(` provides 2 `)`. Since we already consumed one `)`, we now need 1 more `)`. So we increment `insertions` by 1 and set `right_needed` to 1.

At the end of the string, any remaining `right_needed` represents the unmatched `)` that we must insert to balance the remaining open parentheses.



Approach: We use a greedy approach with a single pass to count the required insertions and the number of right parentheses needed.
Time: O(N) where N is the length of the string.
Space: O(1) auxiliary space.

2089.title: Find Target Indices After Sorting Array
2089.notes:
Approach: Count the number of elements strictly smaller than target and the number of elements equal to target; the target indices in the sorted array will be a contiguous range starting from the count of smaller elements.
Time: O(N)
Space: O(1)

2333.title: Minimum Sum of Squared Difference
2333.notes:
Approach:
We compute the absolute differences between `nums1` and `nums2` and count their frequencies using a bucket array, since the maximum difference is at most $10^5$. We then greedily decrement the largest differences using our budget of $k = k1 + k2$ operations. Finally, we calculate the sum of the squared remaining differences.

Time: O(N + M) where N is the length of the arrays and M is the maximum possible difference (10^5).
Space: O(M) to store the frequencies of the differences.

2357.title: Make Array Zero by Subtracting Equal Amounts
2357.notes:
Approach: Count the number of unique positive elements in nums, as each operation can eliminate the smallest unique positive element.
Time: O(N)
Space: O(N)

2409.title: Count Days Spent Together
2409.notes:
Approach:
Convert each "MM-DD" date string to a 1-indexed day of the year using the month lengths of a non-leap year. The overlap between Alice's and Bob's stays is then the range between the maximum arrival day and the minimum departure day.

Time: O(1)
Space: O(1)

2778.title: Sum of Squares of Special Elements

2897.title: Apply Operations on Array to Maximize Sum of Squares
2897.notes:
Approach: Bitwise operations allow shifting set bits across numbers to construct larger numbers. We count the frequency of set bits at each position and construct the $k$ largest possible numbers by greedily placing set bits into the top elements.
Time: O(N * B + K * B) where N is length of nums, K is given integer, and B = 30 is the number of bits.
Space: O(B) = O(1) auxiliary space to store bit counts.

3551.title: Minimum Swaps to Sort by Digit Sum
3551.notes:
Approach: Compute digit sums, pair each element with its digit sum and original index, and sort to find the target permutation. Then, count the number of disjoint permutation cycles to compute the minimum swaps required as the sum of `(cycle_size - 1)`.
Time: O(N log N)
Space: O(N)

3619.title: Count Islands With Total Value Divisible by K
3619.notes:
Approach:
We traverse the grid and use iterative Breadth-First Search (BFS) to explore each unvisited island (cells with value > 0). While exploring an island, we mark visited cells by setting their grid value to 0 and sum up all cell values in the island, then check if the total sum is divisible by $k$.

Time: O(m * n)
Space: O(m * n)

3644.title: Maximum K to Sort a Permutation
3644.notes:
Approach: Every misplaced element must participate in swaps, so $k$ must be a submask of all misplaced elements, making their bitwise AND $K$ the upper bound. Since $K \in [0, n-1]$ exists in the permutation and satisfies $x \text{ AND } K = K$ for all misplaced $x$, $K$ acts as a universal pivot to sort the array, making $K$ the maximum valid answer.
Time: O(n)
Space: O(1)

3723.title: Maximize Sum of Squares of Digits

3727.title: Maximum Alternating Sum of Squares
3727.notes:
Approach:
To maximize the alternating sum of squares, we assign the $\lceil n / 2 \rceil$ largest squared values to positive (even-indexed) positions and the remaining $\lfloor n / 2 \rfloor$ smallest squared values to negative (odd-indexed) positions. We accomplish this by computing the square of each element, sorting them, and subtracting the sum of the smaller half from the sum of the larger half.

Time: O(n log n)
Space: O(n)
